Theorem
[Existence of solution] ↗ def:fractional-sobolev-space ↗ def:fourier-transform-l1 1. ch7:7.3-thm-5\group Hyperbolic Systems

Assume \[ \mathbf{g} \in H^s(\mathbb {R}^n; \mathbb {R}^m) \quad \left(s > \frac{n}{2} + m\right). \] Then there is a unique solution $\mathbf{u} \in C^1([0, \infty ); \mathbb {R}^m)$ of the initial-value problem (32), (33).

Proof

\sketch Fourier transformation changes the PDE into an ODE $\hat u_t+iA(\xi )\hat u=\hat f$. Hyperbolicity diagonalizes $A(\xi )$ with real spectrum and uniform estimates; solve the ODE, bound the weighted Fourier norm, and invert the transform.

□
